question:
A marketing team wants to generate a set of lifestyle photos placing an existing, specific product (shown in one reference photo) into several different generated scenes described by short text prompts.

Which generation approach should they use?

options.text: An image-generation model that accepts a text prompt and a reference image together, so each new scene is generated around the actual product shown in the reference photo.
A text-to-image model, describing the product's appearance in the text prompt in as much detail as the team can write.
A video-generation model, extracting one still frame from the generated clip for each scene.
An OCR model run on the reference photo to extract any text printed on the product's packaging.

explanation:
Passing both the **text prompt and the reference image** to an image-generation model conditions the output on the real product's actual appearance, letting the team place the same real product into many new scenes without it drifting into a generic look-alike.

**Why not the other options:**
- **Text-only description** — No amount of written detail reproduces an exact product's precise shape, color, and branding as reliably as actually providing the reference image to a model built to use it.
- **A video model with frame extraction** — Optimized for temporal video coherence, not single-image product fidelity, and it's an unnecessarily indirect way to produce still images.
- **OCR on the reference photo** — Extracts printed text only; it says nothing about generating a new scene and does not use the photo as visual generation input at all.
